note: Adapted from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English and the genus has no soldier caste, only the alate and worker being described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A medium-sized species, morphologically close to the members of species group I. It differs from A. amicus in the proportionally longer postclypeus and the shorter apical tooth of the mandibles; A. comis is distinguished by the marked differences in the proportions of the mandibular teeth and by the enteric characters of the worker; in A. eumenus the meso- and metanotum are narrower and the apical tooth longer. Among group II, the alate of A. hapalus is rather similar to this species but is larger, with a wider meso- and metanotum and a more strongly inflated postclypeus, and its worker has a longer apical tooth and a much more strongly inflated postclypeus. A. mitis is also distinguished, although its alate postclypeus is not more inflated. A. murcus, which occurs at the same localities, is much smaller and has characteristic long head hairs. Some alates of A. brevior (group III) resemble this species but are usually much darker, have a distinct transverse suture on the meso- and metanotum, differ in the proportions of the mandibular teeth, and their worker has more distinctive mandibular characters and an almost sessile enteric valve seating. Whether the abdomen of the worker dehisces is not known.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow, pilosity concolorous, filiform, inconspicuous but rather dense. Postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.25, Pcl/Ry 1.91; apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.54, Ra/Ri 0.74; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a wide notch, compound ratio 12.45; first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly posterior to the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, the anterior edges of the marginal teeth about equal in length, compound ratio 15.91. Fore tibia weakly inflated, Ti/Ty 4.47, third apical spur small but not reduced, about one third the size of the other two. Junction of mesenteron and proctodaeum oblique, to the right of the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating lateral in the undissected abdomen, the two outer lobes well developed, the third lobe reduced, connected to the second proctodaeal pouch by a rather long neck; membranous wall of the valve with sparse spinules outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown, not darkened above the ocelli; fontanelle short-oval, less than half the size of the ocellus, slightly depressed, pale brown; mid-spot oval, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, brown; postclypeus pale brown, labrum pale yellow; frontal mark a small, rather indistinct, flat pale brown crescent; antennae pale yellowish brown. Pronotum yellowish brown, meso- and metanotum pale yellowish brown, transverse suture absent on the mesonotum and very weak on the metanotum; femora yellowish brown, tibiae pale yellow, tarsi yellowish white. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles pale yellowish brown, sternites and ventral spiracles paler; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli small, separated from the compound eye by about two-thirds of their own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.26, Pcl/Ra 3.42–3.68, posterior margin slightly undulate, median suture weak. Apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.41–0.53, Ra/Rj 0.62–0.65; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, compound ratio 7.50–8.75; apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible in the same line, the anterior edge of the first marginal tooth longer than that of the second. Pilosity of head capsule pale yellowish brown, uneven, not felted. Constriction between meso- and metanotum less narrow, M/W 0.26–0.27. Third apical spur of fore tibia only slightly smaller than the other two.
